purpose: Record a local code, evidence, narrative and public-release-readiness audit for Project One.
scope: Repository readiness review only; no commit, publication, or new OCR evaluation was performed.

original_study.summary: A 14/48, B 31/48, C 7/48, N 5/48 strict scalar matches; score outputs were byte-for-byte unchanged when regenerated after integrity checks.

audit_changes: Made annotation integrity checks explicit so Python optimization cannot remove them; added duplicate-page/target, source identity, bounds, reference-separation and exact-coverage checks.
Required model inventory byte counts as well as SHA-256 matches.
Hardened comparison generation to reject failed or partial runs, missing/duplicate targets, altered score files, incomplete page coverage and mismatched OCR render hashes.
Added a separate score-artifact finalizer to preserve the historical benchmark runner and add hashes for evaluation.json and scoring.log.
Added regression coverage for model sizes, duplicate annotation pages, failed benchmark indexes and score-artifact tampering.
Added a pinned RapidOCR test dependency set and documented the test command.
Revised portfolio narrative to first person while disclosing Codex-assisted development/annotation and same-annotator verification; excluded internal audit notes and execution logs from Git.

Made the static annotation serializer disclose that it does not perform the second visual pass and refuse to run after a freeze; sanitized environment notes and reconciled the prior revision record with all changed frozen files.

pytest.post_exit_warning: Non-fatal pyreadline3 cleanup warning; process exit remained 0.

freeze_divergence.consequence: The original evaluation outputs remain preserved, but the current tree fails the original source-freeze check. A new OCR comparison needs a separately versioned source snapshot and results directory.

release_gaps: No clean-checkout reproduction has been completed.
No source/dependency/model license and notice inventory has been completed; the repository has no project license file.
References have no independent human adjudication, so claims remain limited to this same-annotator-checked sample.
The working tree has no Git commits; no public release or publication occurred.
